Watts made this hymn from Psalm 36:1–2, 5–7, 9, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1An oracle is in my heart regarding the transgression of the wicked man: There is no fear of God before his eyes. 2For his eyes are too full of conceit to detect or hate his own sin. 5Your loving devotion, O LORD, reaches to the heavens, Your faithfulness to the clouds. 6Your righteousness is like the highest mountains; Your judgments are like the deepest sea. O LORD, You preserve man and beast. 7How precious is Your loving devotion, O God, that the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings! 9For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light. PSALM 36:1–2, 5–7, 9 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 36
